Modern.brandNameRationale: Voltgrid compounds voltage and grid. Two syllables, tech-network register. Reads modern, infrastructural, and clear — the network the grid runs into.
Modern.industrySummary: EV charging networks in 2025+ are differentiated by uptime, payment friction, and grid integration. The opening is for a modern operator with clean software, plain pricing, and visible grid-interconnect engineering.
Modern.competitorLandscape: ChargePoint (chargepoint.com) holds the broad-network peer. EVgo (evgo.com) sits in the DC fast peer. Electrify America (electrifyamerica.com) is the high-mileage reference. We sit closer to ChargePoint in modern posture.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern DC fast charging network with clean software and grid-aware pricing.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: J1772 is the SAE connector standard for AC EV charging in North America — the literal physical interface every non-Tesla EV uses. Works carries the heritage workshop register (Powell Works, Steinway Works) and signals the brand is a working operation, not a startup. The whole name reads as a charging network that knows the standards cold.
Corporate.industrySummary: EV charging in 2025+ is split between proprietary networks (Tesla, EVgo) and open-standard networks built on J1772 / CCS. There is a clear opening for a network that anchors itself in the SAE standard tradition — reliable, interoperable, plain.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: EVgo (evgo.com) holds the public-DC-fast slot. ChargePoint (chargepoint.com) sits in the broad-network peer tier. Electrify America (electrifyamerica.com) is the high-mileage standard reference. We sit closer to ChargePoint in posture, with a heritage register.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A J1772/CCS charging network operated by people who know the standards.
